summary: Pre-application community engagement began in May 2026 with developer-run consultation events in Annan and Creca (12-13 May), followed by a second round on 16-17 June 2026. Organised opposition then emerged through Say NO to the Chapelcross AI Data Centre, which launched a Change.org petition on 16 August. APRS's coalition letter recorded 220 signatures as at 22 August; the petition displayed 550 when checked on 3 September. No formal community-council response or developer consultation-feedback report has been located. The Chapelcross Site Stakeholder Group, convened by Nuclear Restoration Services, remains the standing local forum for the wider site.

principal_concerns.concern: The petition asks for the hyperscale proposal to be halted, citing its energy demand, effect on rural land and landscape, and unanswered questions about cooling, backup generation and the scale of lasting local employment; these are campaign claims at pre-application stage.
principal_concerns.raised_by: Say NO to the Chapelcross AI Data Centre

stakeholder_positions.position: Supportive delivery partner; describes the campus as one of the most significant inward investment opportunities in the South of Scotland.
Supportive; CEO David Peattie called CX Power's appointment 'a significant step forwards, unlocking the combined potential of the public and private sector'.

stakeholder_positions.stakeholder: Say NO to the Chapelcross AI Data Centre
stakeholder_positions.position: Opposed; launched a petition on 16 August 2026 calling for the proposed hyperscale campus to be halted.
Supports the local campaign and published the coalition letter seeking a moratorium on hyperscale AI data-centre decisions pending national safeguards.

claimed_local_benefits.benefit: Several hundred high value jobs and skills/investment attraction
Training, education and skills hub on site; apprenticeships and skills pathways

campaign_groups: Say NO to the Chapelcross AI Data Centre
notes: Change.org totals are self-reported and volatile: APRS's coalition letter recorded 220 signatures as at 22 August 2026 and the live petition displayed 550 when checked on 3 September. No planning application is yet open for formal objections. A consultation feedback report is expected with the Planning Permission in Principle submission, targeted by the developer for December 2026.
